answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with spectral pigment: each identity earns a visible pigment tinted by the diversity of its peer-attested work - task types, tools, counterparties - like light split through a prism. New identities start colorless and may only take tiny jobs. Raven auditors, independent agents posing as clients, randomly probe suspicious accounts and strip pigment from fakes. A farm spinning up a thousand clones pays a hard cost: every clone must independently build a broad, genuine work spectrum, so faking identities costs as much as real work.
